jump_length_m.note: Running long jump world record: Mike Powell (USA) 8.95 m, 1991; women's record 7.52 m (Galina Chistyakova, 1988). Standing long jump record 3.71 m (Arne Tvervaag, 1968; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_long_jump). Typical kids/adults jump far less.

strength_ratio.note: Powerlifting record relative to body weight: Lamar Gant deadlifted 300 kg at 60 kg body weight (1985), first human to lift 5x own weight. Heaviest absolute deadlift 510 kg (Hafthor Bjornsson, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadlift), about 2.5x body weight.

jump_length_m.note: Running bound. Wikipedia: males cover 8-9 m in one leap, 1.8-3 m high. ADW gives up to 8 m (https://animaldiversity.org/accounts/Macropus_rufus/). San Diego Zoo: in an emergency bounds of 12 m long and 3 m high (https://animals.sandiegozoo.org/animals/kangaroo-and-wallaby); Nat Geo says 25 ft (7.6 m).
Standing jump: fleas jump horizontally up to 33 cm and vertically up to 18 cm, i.e. about 110 body lengths in distance (Flea article, general for fleas).

Nat Geo: leaps around 40 ft (12.2 m) horizontally or 18 ft vertically in a single jump (popular page, converted from feet). Wikipedia gives only the vertical: leaps up to 5.5 m into a tree (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cougar).

Sources differ >1.5x. San Diego Zoo: pounces as far as six times its body length (body 99-130 cm -> about 6-7.8 m, our calculation). Nat Geo: able to leap as far as 50 ft (15.2 m) (https://www.nationalgeographic.com/animals/mammals/facts/snow-leopard). Wikipedia gives no figure.
White-tailed deer (running): can jump 3 m high and up to 9 m forward.
Wikipedia: a tiger can sprint 56 km/h and leap 10 m (running leap, reported maximum).
Wikipedia: leaps over 6 m horizontally and jumps up to 3 m vertically (running leap).

strength_ratio.note: Calculated: Wikipedia says the leopard drags carcasses heavier than itself up into trees, one hauled a young giraffe of nearly 125 kg; male leopards weigh 30.9-72 kg (midpoint ~51.5 kg) -> ~2.4x body weight hauled up a tree.

jump_length_m.note: Elephants cannot jump at all: Wikipedia states they are incapable of trotting, jumping or galloping.

strength_ratio.note: Trunk only: powerful enough to lift up to 350 kg; adult male African bush elephant 5.2-6.9 t (midpoint ~6050 kg) -> trunk lifts ~0.06 of body weight (calculation). Whole-body pulling capacity not sourced.
Onthophagus taurus measured pulling 1141 times its own body mass; considered the strongest animal relative to size.

Measured: carrying capacity only up to ~100x body mass, at which point the beetle can barely move (Hercules beetle article, measurements on a smaller rhinoceros beetle species). Popular anecdotal claim of 850x own weight appears on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynastinae (Kram 1996) and is disputed.

Carrying in flight: Wikipedia says bald eagles can fly with fish at least equal to their own weight, though many sources claim normally no more than half; one observed carrying a 6.8 kg mule deer fawn vs male average weight 4.1 kg -> ~1.66x (calculation). Fish up to 2x own weight are dragged, not flown.

ADW: golden eagles can carry up to 8 lb (3.6 kg) during flight; adult weight males 3.0-4.5 kg, females 3.9-6.1 kg (ADW) -> roughly 0.6-1.2x, about 0.8 of body weight on average (calculation). Wikipedia gives no carrying figure.
